elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance on expiry or termination
elements.evidence: Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement ... Contractor shall (i) at Company's request, provide reasonable transition assistance

elements.element: Transition assistance available for up to 6 months
Return of Customer Data within 30 days of expiry/termination
elements.evidence: within thirty (30) days of such expiry or termination, return to Company all Works, Confidential Information and other Company data and materials

elements.element: Return in a standard machine-readable format
elements.evidence: in a commonly used, machine-readable format — the playbook's express "standard machine-readable format" wording is not used
(iii) thereafter delete such Company data and materials from its systems
certify such deletion to Company in writing
transition assistance for up to six (6) months, which exceeds 90 days
within thirty (30) days of such expiry or termination, return to Company all Works ... and other Company data and materials

reasons: The inserted paragraph (d) supplies an absent wind-down clause concisely and hits every preferred element except the express "standard machine-readable format" formulation; "commonly used, machine-readable format" is close but is not the playbook's stated standard-format wording.
Fallback is fully satisfied and then some: six months of assistance exceeds 90 days and return runs within 30 days of expiry or termination, not from a later request.
The request condition attaches only to transition assistance; the 30-day return, deletion and written certification are unconditional and sequenced correctly (delete and certify after return).

Minimal: a single short inserted paragraph for a clause that did not exist, with no rewrite of the existing termination, final-payment or Works-assignment sentences and no new exceptions or undefined terms.
Actionable fix to reach preferred: change "commonly used, machine-readable format" to "standard machine-readable format".
